_doc: Classification rules. Edit freely: no code changes needed.
match: folder/file path pattern, '/' separated, case-insensitive.
Leading '/' anchors at the drive root ('/Windows'). Without it the pattern
matches the END of any path ('AppData/Local/Temp', 'node_modules').
'*' inside a component matches any text ('/Users/*/Downloads', '/$*').
cat: apps | media | docs | dev | ai | system | temp | downloads | cloud | other.
safety: green (safe to clear) | yellow (check first) | red (don't touch). Omit if unsure.
protect: tree (this and everything inside can't be deleted from DiskRoot) | self (only this item).
weak: true lets file-extension rules re-classify files inside (e.g. videos on the Desktop).
Extensions: strong=true wins even inside strong folders (model files are always AI).
app: programs using the place; the delete dialog warns while one runs.
action: a Windows tool for the place: dism-cleanup | system-protection | storage-settings.
apps_only: true for bare names projects use too ('Cache'): safe only inside app data, 'check first' elsewhere.
markers: a folder holding a file with this name ('Cargo.toml') or extension ('*.sln') is classified by the marker,
only in your own places (not inside node_modules, Program Files, ...). Earlier markers win. rebuild: child folders
the project's tools rebuild ('bin', 'obj'), marked 'Build output' (safe to clear) with rebuild_note.

rules.note: Windows itself. Never delete files here by hand: use Settings > Storage > Cleanup recommendations or Disk Cleanup.
Windows component store. Much of its apparent size is hardlinks shared with C:\Windows. Shrink safely with: Dism /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup
Needed to repair and uninstall programs. Deleting files here breaks uninstallers.
System temp files. Clear with Disk Cleanup or Storage Sense (needs admin).
Downloaded updates. Disk Cleanup > 'Windows Update Cleanup' removes old ones.
Virtual memory. Its size is set in System > About > Advanced system settings > Performance.
Saved RAM for hibernate and Fast Startup. 'powercfg /h off' (admin) removes it and disables hibernation.
Used by Store apps for paging. Managed by Windows.
System Restore points and volume shadow copies. Manage in System Protection settings (or 'vssadmin').
Deleted files waiting in the Recycle Bin. Empty it from the Recycle Bin itself.
Your previous Windows installation, kept for about 10 days after an upgrade so you can go back. Remove it with Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s).
Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or update. Remove them with Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files (Windows Update Cleanup / temporary Windows installation files).
Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or update. Remove them with Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files (Windows Update Cleanup / temporary Windows installation files).
Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or update. Remove them with Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files (Windows Update Cleanup / temporary Windows installation files).
Temporary files from a Windows upgrade or update. Remove them with Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files (Windows Update Cleanup / temporary Windows installation files).
Files left from a 'Reset this PC' attempt. Remove them with Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files.
File system bookkeeping ($MFT, $LogFile, ...). Managed by NTFS.
Windows recovery environment.
Shared data of installed programs.
Windows and Defender data.
Installer copies kept to repair or uninstall programs (Visual Studio, SDKs...).
Docker data. Clean with 'docker system prune'.
Installed programs. Remove them with Settings > Apps > Installed apps, not by deleting folders.
Installed 32-bit programs. Remove them with Settings > Apps > Installed apps.
Microsoft Store apps. Uninstall from Settings > Apps.
Steam games. Uninstall from the Steam library so Steam knows.
Pre-compiled shaders. Rebuilt automatically when games run.
Epic Games titles. Uninstall from the Epic Games Launcher.
Xbox app games. Uninstall from the Xbox app.
Your downloads. Old installers and archives here are usually safe to remove; check first.
Synced with OneDrive: deleting here also deletes it in the cloud. Use 'Free up space' to keep it online-only instead.
Settings and data of your apps.
Temporary files. Anything not in use is safe to delete; Storage Sense can do it automatically.
Programs installed just for you (VS Code, Python, ...). Uninstall from Settings > Apps.
A WSL Linux distribution and its virtual disk. Remove with 'wsl --unregister <name>' (deletes the distro!).
Docker Desktop data, including its WSL disk (docker_data.vhdx). Clean with 'docker system prune -a', then compact the disk.
Chrome profiles: bookmarks, passwords, history. Clear cache from Chrome settings instead.
Edge profiles. Clear cache from Edge settings instead.
Adobe media cache (conformed audio, previews). Rebuilt when a project is opened; also clearable in Premiere's Media Cache settings.
Adobe media cache database. Rebuilt when a project is opened.
Spotify's music cache. It may also hold songs downloaded for offline listening, which would need downloading again.
Spotify's data cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Discord's cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Discord's script cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Data and caches of classic Microsoft Teams. If you use the new Teams, this can usually go.
Chrome's cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Chrome's script cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Edge's cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Edge's script cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Brave's cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Firefox's cache. Rebuilt automatically.
AMD DirectX shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
AMD DirectX shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
AMD Vulkan shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
NVIDIA DirectX shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Memory dumps from crashed apps. Only useful for debugging those crashes.
Windows Error Reporting files. Disk Cleanup > 'Windows error reports' clears them too.
Go build cache. Clear with: go clean -cache
Composer cache. Clear with: composer clear-cache
Bun cache. Clear with: bun pm cache rm
Deno cache. Clear with: deno clean
Browser cache. Rebuilt automatically.
Cached data. Apps rebuild it when needed.
Cached data. Apps rebuild it when needed.
Compiled script cache. Rebuilt automatically.
GPU shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
NVIDIA DirectX shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
NVIDIA OpenGL shader cache. Rebuilt automatically.
DirectX shader cache. Disk Cleanup can clear it.
Crash reports from apps. Safe to delete.
Thumbnail and icon caches. Disk Cleanup > Thumbnails clears them.
pip download cache. Clear with: pip cache purge
npm cache. Clear with: npm cache clean --force
uv cache. Clear with: uv cache clean
Yarn cache. Clear with: yarn cache clean
pnpm store (shared by projects). Prune with: pnpm store prune
NuGet cache. Clear with: dotnet nuget locals all --clear
NuGet packages. Clear with: dotnet nuget locals all --clear
Maven repository. Re-downloaded on the next build.
Gradle home: caches and wrappers. '.gradle/caches' can be deleted; it is rebuilt.
Gradle caches. Rebuilt on the next build.
Rust crates cache. Re-downloaded when needed.
Rust toolchains. Remove old ones with: rustup toolchain list / uninstall
Android SDK. Remove unused system images and emulators in Android Studio's SDK Manager.
Emulator disks. Delete unused ones in Android Studio's Device Manager.
JetBrains IDE caches and indexes. Old IDE versions' folders can go.
JavaScript dependencies of a project. Safe to delete; 'npm install' brings them back.
A Git repository's full history. Deleting it loses all commits that aren't pushed.
Python virtual environment. Recreate with: python -m venv + pip install -r requirements.txt
Python virtual environment. Recreate with: uv sync / pip install.
Compiled Python bytecode. Recreated automatically.
Anaconda. Clean with: conda clean --all
Miniconda. Clean with: conda clean --all
Downloaded models and datasets. Remove unused ones with: huggingface-cli delete-cache
PyTorch Hub downloads. Re-downloaded when needed.
Local LLMs. Remove with: ollama rm <model>
LM Studio models. Delete unused ones from LM Studio's My Models page.

markers.note: Build or cache output: it carries the standard CACHEDIR.TAG marker (e.g. Rust's target folder). The tool that made it rebuilds it (cargo build, ...).
Python virtual environment (it holds pyvenv.cfg). Recreate it from the project's requirements (pip install -r requirements.txt, uv sync, ...).
A downloaded AI model (Hugging Face layout: tokenizer and weights). Delete it if you no longer use the model; it can be downloaded again.
An Unreal Engine project: your work. Intermediate and DerivedDataCache inside are rebuilt by the editor.
markers.rebuild_note: Unreal Engine rebuilds this folder (Intermediate / DerivedDataCache) the next time the project opens; the first open after deleting it is slower.
